bullets.title: Market sells off on oil spike, rising yields, and weak Treasury buyback
bullets.body: S&P 500 fell 0.48% (breadth 4:1 negative, worst since June 17), NDX -0.3%, RTY -1.3%. Brent crude topped $100/barrel for the first time since July on US-Iran escalation, 10Y Treasury yields rose 5bps to 4.84% (highest since Oct 2023), and a $6B Treasury buyback in the 10-20yr sector disappointed markets expecting up to $10B. Over 80% of S&P 500 stocks closed lower.

bullets.title: CPI Friday is the pivotal macro event; JPM sees 63% odds of 25bp Sep 16 hike
bullets.body: JPM's Feroli projects core CPI +0.21% (vs 0.2% consensus) and headline +0.38%; a 0.2% core print would support dovish interpretation while 0.3%+ risks a hawkish hold. Bond market is pricing ~63% probability of a 25bp hike at the Sep 16 FOMC. PPI preview drops Thursday at 8:30am ET with Feroli expecting +0.2% final demand (5.0% oya). JPM remains tactically cautious/neutral with a risk/reward skewed to the upside on a dovish CPI print.

bullets.title: S&P 500 equity risk premium at 2.1%, lowest since 2002 — bonds increasingly competitive
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags the S&P 500 ERP has compressed to 2.1%, 100bp below historical averages and the lowest reading since 2002, implying higher equity sensitivity to bond yields and growing rebalancing incentive from equities to bonds. Non-bank investors globally are most overweight equities vs. bonds since 2002; G4 pensions and insurers are significantly overweight equities. RBC strategists separately warn of a potential 10% US stock pullback amid election and geopolitical uncertainty.

bullets.title: META +6.6% on Muse AI agent launch; only major tech name to close green
bullets.body: META surged 6.6% on the release of Muse, a consumer AI agent that automates tasks like emails, scheduling, and shopping — making it the standout performer in an otherwise weak tape. The S&P 500 IT Index ended -0.2%, with internet names down 1.1%, software -0.5%, and semis +0.4%. AAPL was flat after unveiling the foldable iPhone Duo at its product event.

bullets.title: Apple unveils foldable iPhone Duo at $1,999 and iPhone 18 Pro from $1,199
bullets.body: Apple's 'Surprise & Shine' event launched the iPhone Duo foldable (5.4" outer / 7.6" unfolded, titanium frame) at $1,999 with preorders Oct 16 and availability Oct 23. iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 (up $100 y/y), featuring the A20 Pro 2nm chip with a 32-core Neural Engine delivering 2x compute for on-device AI and the largest battery life increase ever (24hrs Pro / 30hrs Pro Max). iOS 27 was also announced.

bullets.title: iPhone 18 launch: carriers offering $1,199 trade-in credits; UBS expects 20bps upgrade rate decline
bullets.body: AT&T and T-Mobile are matching the new $1,199 price with full trade-in credits on premium plans, up from $1,099 last year. UBS expects a 20bps y/y industry upgrade rate decline in 3Q-4Q 2026 driven by T-Mobile and Verizon, with higher pricing expected to weigh on consumer demand. UBS forecasts ~2% wireless service revenue growth and ~3% EBITDA growth for the industry.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler initiates AI semi coverage: NVDA, AMD, AVGO, ARM, MRVL all Overweight
bullets.body: Piper's David O'Connor initiated the AI semiconductor complex with broad Overweight ratings: NVDA at $300 PT (34% upside), AVGO at $460 PT (26% upside), ARM at $320 PT (21% upside), AMD at $600 PT (15% upside), and MRVL at $270 PT (15% upside). INTC was initiated Neutral at $110 PT (4% upside). The sweep reflects broad bullish conviction on the AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: AI-driven HDD storage cycle framed as structurally different with >25% exabyte CAGR through 2030
bullets.body: Both WDC and STX management at the Citi Tech Conference characterized the current cycle as fundamentally different from prior HDD cycles — driven by hyperscale/AI infrastructure rather than PCs/enterprise — with exabyte demand growth visibility extending to 2030-2031. WDC reported price/TB up 18-19% y/y last quarter with further increases expected as drives scale to 44TB+; STX noted HDDs are viable in warm-tier KV cache architectures alongside flash, expanding the addressable use case.

bullets.title: VRT down 10%, industrials sector -1.53% — worst relative performer on the day
bullets.body: The S&P 1500 Industrials index fell 1.53% vs. S&P 500 -0.48%, with the Electricals subsector off 2.8% (VRT -10%), E&Cs -2.4%, and Aerospace/Defense -1.7%. Brent above $100 and rising yields hit capex-sensitive names hard. Wells Fargo downgraded VMC to Underweight and EXP to Equal Weight while upgrading MLM to Overweight, signaling a cautious 2027 aggregate outlook for construction materials.

bullets.title: 10Y at 4.84%, 30Y near 2007 highs; 30-year Treasury auction tomorrow the next catalyst
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5bps to 4.84% (highest since Oct 2023) and the 30-year is near its highest since 2007. JPM expects smooth digestion of the $22B 30-year auction Thursday, noting August's 30-year auction cleared 0.4bp cheap with 88.5% end-user takedown. The 5-year note is rallying toward 4.62-4.65% support with the belly leading the yield rise.

bullets.title: CMCSA -6.6% as CFO guides no improvement in Q3 broadband subscriber losses
bullets.body: Comcast CFO at Goldman's Communacopia conference stated Q3 broadband net subscriber losses will not improve year-over-year, with net adds tracking -87k vs. -91k y/y. The stock was the worst large-cap performer on the day. DOJ also expanded its probe into the Fox-Roku acquisition, weighing on FOXA (-2.1%) and ROKU (-1.6%).

bullets.title: Sector rotation: energy sole gainer; rate-sensitive REITs, utilities, and consumer discretionary lag
bullets.body: Energy was the only S&P sector to close positive as oil surged. REITs fell 1.12% (self-storage -2.35%, office -1.73%, multi-family -1.39%), utilities dropped 1.2% (solar ETF -2.8%), and consumer discretionary fell 1.3%. The 30-year fixed mortgage rose 8bps to 6.97%. The defensive-energy trade was reinforced by Middle East escalation with no visible diplomatic off-ramp.

bullets.title: JPM tactically favors Mag7 near-term, Software if Semis fall; hedging via short credit ETFs, long VIX
bullets.body: Into the Sep 16 Fed meeting, JPM is tactically long Mag7, prefers Software over Semis on a relative basis if the latter weakens, and favors Large-Cap Banks and Consumer Discretionary (contingent on energy pullback). Hedges recommended include short credit ETFs and long VIX. Hedge funds have been adding gross exposure, supporting upside if CPI is benign. Post-midterm election SPX returns historically strong: +5.4% at 3 months (78% hit rate), +11.4% at 6 months (100% hit rate).

bullets.title: AI spending growth stalled in August at +0.4% m/m; agentic AI commerce at ~1 visit per 600 retail visits
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagged slowing AI adoption momentum: enterprise AI tool spending rose just 0.4% month-over-month in August. Separately, Hedgeye data shows AI agents drive only ~1 visit per 600 retail site visits, stalled since April, despite 87 million monthly ChatGPT users in the US. Retail media is flagged as the most exposed profit pool as AI intermediation changes the customer-retailer relationship.

bullets.title: Google to invest $15.1B in Finland AI infrastructure; data center permitting headwinds mounting
bullets.body: Google announced at least $15.1B in Finland AI infrastructure investment over two years. However, a joint Blackstone data center venture encountered permitting and site delays at multiple locations, and data center development was delayed in Massachusetts and Charlotte amid local community opposition — a theme that Morgan Stanley is hosting a dedicated event on Sept 17.

bullets.title: Consumer spending data mixed: credit card data soft but retail traffic improving into September
bullets.body: Citi credit card data showed total spending at -1.4% in Sept week 1 (vs. -5.2% in Aug week 4), partly reflecting Labor Day timing. Apparel was the weakest category (-17.6%), while aftermarket auto parts surged +20.2%. Retail traffic tracker showed +1.7% YoY for Sept week 1, with COST surging mid-teens but CPRI (-19.9%), TPR (-16.3%), and UAA (-17.9%) sharply weaker. Low-income households (<$100K) remain stretched while high-income spending accelerates.

bullets.title: FHFA mandates VantageScore alongside FICO for all Fannie/Freddie MBS — credit scoring duopoly erodes
bullets.body: FHFA Director Bill Pulte announced all Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac MBS, credit risk transfers, and securitized products must carry VantageScore in addition to FICO, representing a direct push toward competition in credit decision-making software and a structural challenge to FICO's dominant position in mortgage origination.

bullets.title: SMid biotech (XBI) +33% YTD vs SPX +12% as FDA operations stabilize under Trump
bullets.body: Citi's biopharma summit notes FDA operations are normalizing with reduced policy unpredictability, driving improved confidence in review timelines. The XBI has outperformed the S&P 500 by ~21 percentage points YTD, reflecting the relief rally in regulatory risk premium across the small/mid biotech universe.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR surged +16.1% YoY in week ended Sept 5; Labor Day shift the primary driver
bullets.body: STR data showed US weekly RevPAR +16.1% YoY (vs. +1.6% prior week), with Vegas Strip +32.5% and economy segment +11.8%. September MTD total US RevPAR is running +21.0% YoY on a same-day basis. The Labor Day calendar shift (Sept 1 in 2025 vs. Sept 7 in 2026) is the primary driver of the spike; underlying economy segment two-year stacks accelerated from -6.7% to +7.1%, suggesting genuine demand improvement beneath the noise.

bullets.title: Macro input cost pressures persist across consumer staples: Clorox guides >$200M FY27 inflation
bullets.body: Conference takeaways from consumer companies show persistent input cost headwinds: Clorox expects >$200M in input cost inflation for FY27 (more than double historical norm), Kraft Heinz anticipates 4-5% cost inflation, and Kimberly-Clark faces $35-40M in spot freight volatility and up to $10M in Canadian retaliatory tariff costs. Cheesecake Factory hit psychological price barriers, holding menu increases under 2%.
